entries.subject: DAMIT 4281: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-4281.txt. Model 4281, version 2019-05-07, pole (237°, 57°), period 7.69659 h match the retained metadata. The archive supplies no diameter for this model; a separate scale constraint is required. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: NEOWISE Gr12b: selected thermal size
entries.finding: The original IRSA query was rerun for asteroid 3451; its Gr12b row matches the retained diameter 126.2880 km, error 1.6420 km, fit code DVBI and mean epoch 2455324.0991095. D in FIT_CODE means diameter was fitted. This effective-sphere diameter provides an approximate display scale, not a resolved surface or an independent physical-volume fit to the shape.

entries.subject: Shape and spin alternatives
entries.finding: The grid marks unmapped coverage: no registered global reflectance mosaic was found in the selected releases. Convex inversion leaves concavities and fine relief unresolved. - Transferring thermal diameter to mesh volume is approximate. The quoted fit error excludes additional thermal/shape uncertainty and does not measure local shape accuracy. - Elevation is false color for model radius minus a reference sphere, not gravitational height or independent terrain. - Absolute phase is arbitrary; accelerated display spin is illustrative. Orbit context is fixed at 2026-09-03 TT. The archive also lists an alternative pole. - Hanuš et al. (2023), [*Shape models and spin states of Jupiter Trojans: Testing the streaming instability formation scenario*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.05380v1), Table B.2 revises the shape/spin solution. The recorded public target query did not expose its numerical mesh; this view keeps the older mesh and matching pole. The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 4282: pole (82°, 7°), 7.69659 h, version 2019-05-07. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numerical replacement or independent pole/size constraints that distinguish the recorded alternatives, followed by comparison against the currently selected model.

entries.subject: Source mesh and calibration preservation
entries.finding: The [original mesh](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/stored_files/open/13357/shape.txt) is retained without changing its coordinates or connectivity. [DAMIT documentation](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/pages/documentation) supplies the coordinate units, pole and sidereal-period conventions; its CC BY 4.0 terms and other credits are linked from NOTICE.md.

entries.subject: Alternative archive solution: model 4282, ecliptic pole (82°, 7°)
entries.revisitWhen: Published model-specific definitions, an independently constrained pole/scale, or a released replacement mesh that resolves the recorded ambiguity.

entries.subject: PDS SBN catalogue values that disagree with the factsheet or are not shown
entries.finding: Small Bodies Occultations V4.0 record 492, DAMIT model 4281 diameter 100 ± 3 km (volume-equivalent; DAMIT model 4281 fitted to 1 occultation) is not shown: the astronomy record takes its size from a publication ("PDS Becker radar meshes: source-volume radii; GM unknown in Horizons."), and it differs from the astronomy record's mean radius 63.144 km (diameter 126.288 km).
entries.revisitWhen: A newer release of the named catalogue, or a review that replaces the shown value.
